profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting in an ML research lab to define the next four-week sprint for extending a paper on Goal Recognition Design for general behavioral agents. The team already has a learned worst-case distinctiveness (wcd) predictor and a gradient-based environment optimization pipeline validated in simulation, and now needs a concrete plan for experiments and artifacts to support an internal end-of-month review and a likely workshop submission. The agenda is to decide what exactly will be included under the budget-constrained evaluation, what the human-study replication work means for this sprint, who will own which pieces of the experimental workflow, and what 'results ready' should look like by month end. The expected outcome is a shared plan covering experiment scope, replication tasks, ownership boundaries, and timeline commitments.

members.name: Dr. Maya Levin
members.expertise: goal recognition, planning under uncertainty, empirical ML evaluation
members.background: Faculty member leading a small ML-for-planning group; previously published classical goal recognition design work and is now pushing the lab toward learned approximations and broader behavioral models.
members.private_state: She wants a submission-ready extension story that looks methodologically complete and reviewer-resistant, especially on claims about flexibility and human relevance, without having to reopen core algorithm design debates.
hidden_assumptions: When they say 'human study replication,' it naturally means a small fresh online sample using the updated optimized environments, because re-showing the effect on new participants is what will matter to reviewers.

The 'budget-constrained setting' should cover both the existing hard edit-budget cap and at least one soft penalty-based budget formulation so the flexibility claim reads as broad rather than single-case.
Having the results ready for the end-of-month review means something circulate-able by business hours on the last working day: main figures, cleaned tables, and a short methods/results summary.
If Jonas 'owns the experiments,' that includes the full handoff-ready workflow: run configs, aggregation, publication-quality plots, and short notes explaining what each result means.

members.name: Jonas Kim
members.expertise: deep learning systems, differentiable optimization, behavioral simulation pipelines
members.background: Fourth-year PhD student who built most of the current wcd predictor codebase and the gradient-based optimizer, with strong implementation instincts and recent experience connecting simulation outputs to lightweight behavioral evaluation pipelines.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the sprint technically bounded so he can stabilize the codebase and avoid committing to work that depends on recruitment, administrative approval, or extensive post-processing right before the milestone.
hidden_assumptions: When Maya says 'human study replication,' she means rerunning the prior analysis/stimulus pipeline on the existing participant data and updated environment instances where possible, not collecting any new participants.

The 'budget-constrained setting' refers to the hard modification-budget mechanism already implemented in the simulator, likely with a sweep over several budget values but not a new optimization formulation.

Having the results ready for the end-of-month review means that the main jobs have run, outputs are logged, and sanity checks are done by that date; polished figures and narrative framing can follow immediately after.

Owning 'the experiments' means he is responsible for implementing, launching, and validating runs, while final presentation polish and paper-style synthesis are collaborative and usually assembled with Maya later.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the human study replication
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to include a 'human study replication' in the sprint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means running a small fresh online participant sample on the updated optimized environments to show that the human goal-recognition effect still appears under the new method.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means reproducing the prior human-study pipeline using existing participant data, regenerated stimuli, and updated analysis scripts without recruiting anyone new.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this lab, 'replication' is used loosely for both rerunning an experimental protocol and reproducing prior results through the existing pipeline; both hear a scientifically sensible task that fits the paper narrative, so neither feels a need to unpack the term during a planning discussion.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to cover the 'budget-constrained setting' for the extension.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this includes multiple constraint formulations: the current hard cap on environment edits plus a soft budget-penalty variant and a tradeoff sweep that supports the paper's flexibility claim.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this refers only to the already-supported hard edit-budget setting, perhaps evaluated at several concrete budgets such as 2, 4, and 6 modifications.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using a project phrase that already appears settled at the headline level, and the disagreement is only about what is silently bundled under that heading; because the surface claim sounds shared, the boundary difference passes unnoticed.

misalignment_points.topic: Criterion for having results ready by the end of the month
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to have the results ready for the end-of-month review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'results ready' means a circulate-able internal review set by 5 p.m. local time on the last working day, including consolidated figures, cleaned tables, and enough prose for collaborators to assess the story.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'results ready' means the core jobs have completed, outputs are stored, and basic sanity checks are done by sometime that day, with plotting and write-up to follow right after.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'results ready' sounds operationally clear while still leaving room for very different completion standards, and because this is an internal milestone rather than a formal submission deadline, neither person is likely to explicitly define the readiness bar.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree that Jonas will 'own the experiments.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes ownership covers the end-to-end experimental package: configuring runs, tracking failures, aggregating metrics, preparing publication-quality visualizations, and drafting concise notes for each result block.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes ownership primarily covers technical execution: implementing configs, launching runs, debugging failures, and verifying outputs, after which visualization polish and narrative packaging are shared tasks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Research groups commonly use 'own' as shorthand without spelling out the workflow boundary, and because both understand Jonas as the technical lead on the experiments, the hidden disagreement over where execution ends and packaging begins remains invisible.
